newsitem.title: GERMANY: Left-wingers hurl bottles, stones at Berlin police.
newsitem.headline: Left-wingers hurl bottles, stones at Berlin police.

text.p: Masked demonstrators hurled stones, bottles and beer cans at Berlin police on Thursday and set fire to two builders' huts, as violence by right-wing and left-wing extremists marred May day rallies across Germany.

Police tried to break up the clashes with batons and water cannons. The trouble followed a demonstration of around 6,500 left-wing extremists in the city and came after hundreds of neo-Nazis rampaged through the northern town of Muenden.

The Berlin left-wingers built barricades out of rubbish bins and vehicles and tore up paving stones to throw at the police in the Prenzlauer Berg area, a focus for May Day protests since the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.

Police gave no details of any injuries or arrests, but said around 50 people had been detained in other clashes. They said around 4,000 officers were on the streets and police in neighbouring Saxony were on standby if the trouble worsened.
"The potential for violence is extremely high," Berlin Interior Minister Joerg Schoenbohn told Berlin radio.
Earlier, hundreds of neo-Nazis and dozens of left-wingers smashed windows and rampaged through the tourist resort of Muenden after police broke up an unauthorised right-wing rally.
Police there said they had detained 150 people in the town and one police officer had been hurt by a flying bottle.

In the eastern city of Leipzig, left-wing extremists hurled rocks and fireworks at police who were trying to keep them apart from a small group of skinheads defying a ban on a rally there. Police detained around 200 people after the clashes.
Thousands of police were on duty in Leipzig and Berlin bracing for such violence as demonstrators gathered for mass May day rallies which have often ended in clashes with police.
Left-wing extremists in Berlin have targeted expensive cars, shops and bars in the past. They went on the rampage 10 years ago on May 1, looting and setting fire to a supermarket.
